UYF

Urban Youth Foundation

Birthed out of
The Urban Playground

The UYF was born out of The Urban Playground to create an environment, a network, a new culture of life-changing experiences for youth and young people. Our goal is to equip disadvantaged South African youth (16–25) with marketable creative and entrepreneurial skills through hands-on mentorship in film production, photography, music, fashion, sports coaching, coding, game development, AI training, event & venue management and small-business development.

Our programme is 12 months, combining theory classes, practical mentorship placements, skills workshops, portfolio-building projects, entrepreneurship training and placement support.

Executive Summary

The ultimate experience
for the youth of today

The Urban Playground is a place where young people express themselves through their passions in a safe, secure environment — the forerunner in a space dedicated entirely to youth and young-adult development, across the sub-cultures we call “expressions.”

Breakdancing, skateboarding and BMXing are joining the Olympic programme — proof that sport is changing, and that the next generation is drawn to disciplines that didn't exist 10 or 20 years ago, like esports.

The Urban Playground brings new-age sports, arts, creativity, tech and gaming together in one expression of street art: an art gallery where basketball, street soccer, parkour, dance, skate and BMX are played, where creatives build podcasts, music and video content for the next generation, and where gamers hone their skills in the fastest-growing industry in the world.

Enter the Urban Playground — the home of the next generation.

Youth Development & Job Creation

Super Playgrounds,
in every major city

We will be opening Super Playgrounds in every major city in South Africa. The key to our success is having the right people — we already have key partners at a high level, and a development plan to train and retain the best staff on the ground.

Our development programme is a mentorship model that teaches theory and skills, with a major practical side: mentees work real scenarios alongside experts in film production, sound production, social media marketing, eventing, photography, journalism, coding, event management, and food & hospitality.

Graduates leave employment-ready — working for us, for one of our partners, or independently with an impressive skills résumé. We're also developing future sports stars in soccer, skateboarding, BMXing, parkour, basketball and dance.

Each venue will need 50+ staff. Once our 5 main venues are established across South Africa, we'll be training over 1,000 people a year.

How It Works

The Youth Development System

01

Touch

The locations set up for regular events naturally become focal points for young people — contact points where we begin to reach them.

02

Engage

With regular contact and registration, a relationship is established and grown.

03

Sustain

With activities, classes, training and workshops, young people explore their potential.

04

Develop

Potential becomes a life skill or career — and through our network of influence, we can channel it further.

05

Channel

These young people go back into the workforce — through our network or other job opportunities — with a full résumé of theory and practical skills.

Context & Need

Why this matters now

Youth unemployment in South Africa remains high, while creative industries present accessible entry points with growing local and digital markets.

Many talented young people lack networks, equipment, practical experience and the financial support and business skills to convert talent into sustainable livelihoods.

Practical mentorships bridge skills-to-work gaps better than classroom-only programmes.

The Gap

High youth unemployment meets accessible, growing creative and digital markets.

The Barrier

Talent without networks, equipment, experience or capital rarely becomes income.

The Bridge

Hands-on mentorship, not classroom theory alone, closes the skills-to-work gap.

We aim to deliver business and digital skills so that 50% of graduates secure paid employment, freelance income, or start a micro-enterprise within 6 months of graduation. The other 50% will be employed by The Urban Playground, Urban Sessions or Urban Collective.

We build transferable skills — project management, client work, teamwork, digital portfolios — and connect youth to industry networks.

Target Beneficiaries & Selection

Who we mentor

Currently we have 26 youth that we are mentoring in 2026. In 2027 we'd like to invite 100 youth aged 16–25 from underserved urban and peri-urban communities.

Selection criteria: a demonstrated interest in one of our creative industries or business areas, basic literacy, financial need, and commitment to the full programme. All applicants require a police clearance and no criminal record, as we work with children and youth.

Inclusion: gender balance, with at least 50% young women.

Mentorship

Current Projects, 2026

Currently we have 26 youth that we are mentoring. We're also working with the City of Joburg to find a building for our Central Development Hub — until then, they've given us a playground in central Joburg and a venue in Soweto.

Every student learns first aid and completes an international barista course (a skill they can use in any country in the world). From there they build foundations in marketing, branding, AI skills and business management, before going deeper into the skillset they choose — media, business, sports coaching, fashion, eventing or app development.

Programme Benefits

Real experience,
real outcomes

We have experts in every field delivering the theory as well as the hands-on practical experience — mentees get real job experience working alongside experts.

This is a 5-day-a-week programme, and mentees aren't just learning — they're working on major projects and building their résumé.

All 26 mentees have been placed for full-time employment for 2027.
